data.name: Solaroids
data.detailed_description:
Enfrenta uma ameaça aparentemente intransponível que persegue o teu precioso sol. Defende o teu sistema solar num conflito contínuo que progride desde simples níveis introdutórios até batalhas espaciais épicas de alta intensidade que desafiarão até os pilotos mais experientes.

Power-Ups


Conforme a campanha avança e a ameaça continua a crescer, o mesmo acontece com os tipos de armas à tua disposição. Executa manobras avançadas enquanto te esquivas de asteroides, minas e mísseis inimigos. Melhora as capacidades da tua nave e acumula pontuações cada vez mais altas. Equipa armas primárias, secundárias e defensivas - a escolha é tua.

Upgrades


Adiciona acessórios adicionais de outrider e cria uma nave poderosa. Mantém a tua nave e outriders em bom estado ou observa os teus preciosos Power-Ups a flutuarem na escuridão do espaço para serem conquistados.

Inimigos


Sob a cobertura de uma cintura de asteroides, poderosos inimigos aguardam pela altura certa para atacar. Cada inimigo tem os seus próprios padrões de ataque, armas e fraquezas. Sê cauteloso e utiliza a cintura de asteroides para os derrotar.

Multijogador Local


Voa sozinho, ou com até três amigos no modo multijogador local. Joga contra ondas de inimigos ou enfreta os teus amigos numa arena aberta. Os jogadores podem juntar-se a qualquer altura sem necessidade de configurar modos de jogo complexos. Personaliza as cores primárias e secundárias e torna a tua nave única. Configura as opções de fogo e colisões amigas para ajustar o nível de cooperação.

Emulação


Simula a experiência das clássicas Máquinas Arcade e consolas retro, ajustando os efeitos do Vetor, Paleta e CRT. Personaliza-os segundo as tuas preferências.

Acesso Antecipado

O meu nome é Chad Yates (Kiates), e quero tornar o Solaroids no melhor jogo de arcade retro 2D estilo Asteroids© do mercado. Pesquisa o meu histórico de atualizações e patches e vê os eventos regulares de pontuações máximas que organizo. Consulta os fóruns e verás o meu nível de compromisso. Junta-te à minha comunidade, sugere alterações e joga as últimas versões do jogo - vamos construir isto juntos!!

O Solaroids continuará a evoluir em Acesso Antecipado com as contribuições dos jogadores da comunidade, até ao seu lançamento oficial!

Características Adicionais

  • Sistema de dano com base em propriedades físicas, mecânicas e elétricas.
  • Até 4 jogadores locais
  • Créditos ilimitados (configurável)
  • Jogo Livre - Prepara-te para uma partida de ação intensa (desbloqueável)
  • Listas separadas de Pontuações Máximas Globais e Locais para Primeiro Crédito e Qualquer Crédito.
  • Banda Sonora Original
  • Suporta música do Steam.
  • Esquemas de controlo totalmente configuráveis: Clássico, Híbrido (um manípulo), Moderno (dois manípulos)
  • Suporta resolução 4K
  • Suporta 60Hz-240Hz+

Atualiza a tua nave e utiliza Power-Ups adicionais. Modo Um Jogador ou até 3 amigos para uma partida de cooperação local intensa.

reviews.review:
Solaroids, developed by Chad Yates and published by DynF/X Digital LLC, is a twin-stick space shooter that takes the timeless foundation established by classic arcade titles and injects it with enough new ideas to feel relevant in the modern era. At first glance, it appears to be another love letter to Asteroids, complete with drifting rocks, neon visuals, and score chasing. However, the longer one spends with the game, the clearer it becomes that Solaroids is attempting to build its own identity through expanded mechanics, environmental hazards, and a steady stream of challenges that keep players engaged long after the first session.

The gameplay revolves around navigating dangerous sectors of space while destroying asteroids, hostile ships, and increasingly formidable bosses. Movement is fluid and precise, which is essential considering how quickly situations escalate. Enemies approach from multiple angles, debris fills the screen, and projectiles can transform a comfortable run into a desperate fight for survival within seconds. The inclusion of multiple control options is a welcome touch, ensuring both veterans of arcade shooters and newcomers can find a setup that feels natural. What elevates the experience is the emphasis on tactical play. Asteroids are not merely targets; they become obstacles to hide behind, tools for evasion, and environmental elements that can influence encounters in meaningful ways.

Solaroids also benefits from its variety. The game introduces power-ups, ship enhancements, and large-scale boss encounters that add welcome shifts in pacing. Boss battles in particular stand out, demanding patience and adaptability instead of simple reflexes. Each encounter encourages players to learn attack patterns and make better use of their arsenal, creating moments that feel rewarding rather than repetitive. Despite its retro inspiration, the game avoids becoming trapped in nostalgia by continually introducing new challenges that push players to refine their strategies.

One of the title's greatest strengths is its replay value. Solaroids embraces the philosophy of classic arcade design, where mastery is the ultimate objective. Leaderboards, achievements, and recurring score competitions provide ample incentive to keep returning. Every failed run feels like a lesson rather than a punishment, and there is a satisfying sense of progression that comes from surviving longer and posting increasingly impressive scores. Players who enjoy chasing personal bests will likely find themselves investing far more time than expected. The developer's continued support over the years further reinforces the impression that Solaroids is a labor of love rather than a disposable indie release.

Multiplayer support adds another dimension to the experience. Local cooperative play for up to four participants transforms the game into a lively and often chaotic event. Coordinating attacks while avoiding hazards creates memorable moments, especially when the screen fills with explosions and enemy fire. While the absence of dedicated online multiplayer may disappoint some players, the inclusion of Remote Play Together helps alleviate that limitation and preserves the communal spirit that inspired many arcade games of the past.

Visually, Solaroids adopts a colorful and energetic presentation that complements its fast-paced action. Particle effects and explosions provide a satisfying spectacle without obscuring important gameplay information. The soundtrack and sound effects do an admirable job of maintaining momentum throughout each session, reinforcing the game's identity as an arcade experience first and foremost. That said, players looking for a strong narrative or deep progression systems may find the package somewhat limited. Solaroids remains firmly committed to gameplay-driven entertainment, and its appeal depends heavily on an appreciation for high-score competition and repeated playthroughs.

In the end, Solaroids succeeds by understanding what made classic space shooters memorable while adding enough modern refinements to justify its existence. It delivers responsive controls, meaningful gameplay variety, and excellent replayability in a package that feels polished and thoughtfully designed. Though its arcade-focused approach will not appeal to everyone, fans of twin-stick shooters and score-based challenges will find plenty to admire. It stands as a testament to how enduring simple concepts can be when executed with creativity and care.

Rating: 7/10
